doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Reaction to others covering his songs
summary: He never thought about it; credit mattered. Bonnie Raitt did the first cover.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Thank you. This is going to sound like a stupid interview question. But how does it make you feel that all these artists, some of the most serious singers and songwriters of the last 30 years, Amy’s generation, my generation, sing your songs and use them as models? Do you have any...
You don’t have any feelings about that?
No. I never thought about it.
I know what you’ve said about.
As long as they give you credit.
You have said...what did you say about Pete Townsend... You said he made “Young Man Blues” sound like an anthem. You said something nice about it.
Well, the Who made everything sound like an anthem.
I remember that you liked Bonnie Raitt’s version of “Everybody Crying Mercy.” He was always I think happy that people would do it.
Happy that they did it, sure.
Bonnie Raitt did the first cover of my song, “Everybody’s Crying Mercy.”
I don’t know when she did that, but...
